evidence.description: The workflow explicitly guards against repeated independent-unit entries: read_vessels raises a ValueError if any vessel_id appears more than once, so duplicated units could not silently enter the test.

source_refs.quoted_text:
def read_vessels(path):
    """Return the CSV rows, refusing any vessel that shows up twice."""
    with path.open("r", encoding="ascii", newline="") as handle:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(handle))
    seen = set()
    for row in rows:
        vessel = row["vessel_id"]
        if vessel in seen:
            raise ValueError("vessel_id appears more than once: " + vessel)
        seen.add(vessel)
    return rows

evidence.description: The selected result's reported statistics are reproducible from one titer per vessel: complete separation of arms (wildtype max 44.5 < engineered min 46.9) gives U = 6*6 = 36 and exact two-sided p = 2/C(12,6) = 2/924 ≈ 0.00216, and arm means 42.00 vs 49.25 g/L give the reported +7.25 g/L gap, confirming the test was run on the 12 vessel-level rows with no unit entering twice.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict by (1) scanning every vessel_id in data/input.csv for repeats — all twelve values V01–V12 are distinct, matching the declared independent-unit column; (2) checking whether the workflow could multiply rows before testing — arm_titers only filters rows by strain_arm and read_vessels rejects duplicates, so no row duplication or expansion occurs upstream of stats.mannwhitneyu; (3) checking whether any other column (inoculum_lot) encodes a repeated unit disguised under distinct vessel_ids — all twelve lot values are unique, and the description states one lot per vessel; and (4) recomputing the reported statistics from the raw data (means 42.00 vs 49.25, complete separation giving U = 36 and exact p = 2/924 ≈ 0.00216), which matches the report exactly and is consistent with exactly one entry per vessel. None of these attempts produced evidence of a repeated independent-unit entry into the row-independent test.
